---
title: "how_to_update_pkg"
author: Wu Yitong
---

This is a brief, rough, informal instruction of how to update this package through CRAN for future maintainers. 

**For details, please refer to https://r-pkgs.org/release.html. Highly recommend to go through this website for the first time maintainers.**

# Step 1: Code, Document, Test

After modifying code, you should also update the document of the function, and also modify the corresponding test under folder "catalytic\\tests\\testthat\\".

For example, below is the original function and corresponding test:

```{r}
library(testthat)

# Original function

#' Calculate two numbers with different methods
#'
#' @param a Numeric. The first number.
#' @param b Numeric. The second number.
#' @param how Method for calculating number `a` and `b`, chose from "add" and "minus".
#'
#' @return Numeric. The result of calculating number `a` and `b`
calculate_a_and_b <- function(a, b, how = c("add", "minus")){
  switch(how,
         "add" = a + b,
         "minus" = a - b)
}

# Corresponding Test
test_that("calculate_a_and_b works correctly", {
  a <- 3
  b <- 2
  
  expect_equal(calculate_a_and_b(a, b, "add"), a + b)
  expect_equal(calculate_a_and_b(a, b, "minus"), a - b)
  expect_null(calculate_a_and_b(a, b, "other_method"))
})
```

And after you modify the code, you should update the document and test:

```{r}
# Original function + new feature (multiply)

#' Calculate two numbers with different methods
#'
#' @param a Numeric. The first number.
#' @param b Numeric. The second number.
#' @param how Method for calculating number `a` and `b`, chose from "add", 
#' "minus" and "multiply".
#'
#' @return Numeric. The result of calculating number `a` and `b`
calculate_a_and_b <- function(a, b, how = c("add", "minus", "multiply")){
    switch(how,
         "add" = a + b,
         "minus" = a - b,
         "multiply" = a * b)
}

# Corresponding Test
test_that("calculate_a_and_b works correctly", {
  a <- 3
  b <- 2
  
  expect_equal(calculate_a_and_b(a, b, "add"), a + b)
  expect_equal(calculate_a_and_b(a, b, "minus"), a - b)
  expect_equal(calculate_a_and_b(a, b, "multiply"), a * b) # NEW TEST
  expect_null(calculate_a_and_b(a, b, "other_method"))
})
```

# Step 2: Run Test

To ensure the code you changed will NOT influence other part of code, you should save all the document and run all the test and see **ALL** the test pass.

```{r}
devtools::document() # Save the changes of document
devtools::test() # Run all the test
```

# Step 3: State your changes

Now, all code can run, all document saved, all test passed. 

Then, you should let users and CRAN know what you changed.

## 1. NEWS.md

This file is intended for **USERS**. Your package users will read NEWS.md to know what you changed for each version. So, keep the statement in NEWS.md short and straightforward, there is no need to write coding details in this file.

Now, open file NEWS.md, you might see something like:

```
# catalytic 0.1.1

* Some updates ...


# catalytic 0.1.0

* Initial release.
```

You can call `usethis::use_release_issue()`, you’ll be asked which type of release version you intend to make.

```{r}
usethis::use_release_issue()
```

Now, if it is a patch fix, a small change or a bug fix. You can write below on top of all NEWS:

```
# catalytic 0.1.2

* Fix bug on ...


```

If it is minor changes, some bugs, some small feature added. You can write below on top of all NEWS:

```
# catalytic 0.2.0

* Added functionality to ...


```

Or, if it is a major change, you added a big block of code for new feature, with proper test and vignettes. You can write below on top of all NEWS:

```
# catalytic 1.0.0

* Enable to ...


```

## 2. DESCRIPTION

- Update the release version to keyword `Version`.

- Add your name (if it is a significant change) to keyword `Authors@R`.

## 3. inst/CITATION

- Add your name to the file (if it is a significant change) to keyword `author`.

# Step 4: CRAN Check

Now, package looks complete.

Finally, we go through all the checks determined in website: https://r-pkgs.org/release.html.


## 2. cran-comments.md

This file is intended for **CRAN**. This file is for you to tell CRAN. 

Kindly check website for details: https://r-pkgs.org/release.html.
